_why: Mystery Player answers must be people known FIRST as footballers. Alex, 2026-08-14: 'some players go into management yes, but it is a bit misleading if some players had a way bigger career as a manager than as a player. Xavi, Xabi Alonso are good mystery players — they are managers nowadays but known as great footballers. Alex Ferguson also played at a high level but everyone knows him as a manager, so he would not fit.' The pool carries no occupation field and FAME CANNOT SEPARATE THESE — Ferguson scores 113, higher than Platini — so this list is curated by hand and is the only reliable filter.
_ruling: Alex, 2026-08-14: '95% players and the rest managers — focus on current players but sprinkle in these managers that have played, but rarely. Zidane and Pep Guardiola are both fine as well, but Mourinho, Ferguson etc are not okay.' So there are two lists, not one.
_method: The names were not guessed. scripts/verify-mystery-answers.mjs checks all 606 curated answers against Wikidata — P106 occupation, P54 playing spells, P6087 coaching spells — and reports anyone who coached longer than they played. That found 29. The extremes split cleanly on ratio; the middle was Alex's call, because the rule is about FAME and no field encodes fame.
_managers_note: HARD BAN. Known as managers, full stop. Ferguson played 15 years and coached 40; Eriksson played 5 and coached 40; Mourinho played 8 and coached 27. Never scheduled.
_rationed_note: ALLOWED BUT CAPPED at MANAGER_QUOTA in gen-mystery-schedule.mjs (5% of days). Real players whose managing later outgrew their playing fame. Good answers occasionally, wrong as a staple.
_explicitly_fine_note: Named by Alex or cleared by the Wikidata ratio. Guardiola is NOT flagged by the check at all — his playing years match his coaching years — which contradicted an earlier cautious hand-exclusion of mine. Zidane was never flagged.
_notFootballers_note: O. J. Simpson was in the CURATED ANSWER SET at fame 61 with club 'Buffalo Bills'. American football. He would have been served as a daily football puzzle. Not an editorial judgement — a data error, and the reason this file also carries a hard sport check. Julio Iglesias was caught the same way, during the manager sweep: a Real Madrid youth goalkeeper before a car crash ended it, in the answer set at fame level with club 'Real Madrid Club de Fútbol'. Famous-for-something-else is its own failure mode, separate from managers, and neither fame nor club can detect it.
